instruction: Create a custom keybinding "ctrl+shift+f" to open the file explorer when the sidebar is not visible in VS Code.

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a VSCode keyboard shortcut ctrl+shift+f to open the file explorer when the sidebar is not visible. Uses existing check_json_keybindings function to verify the keybinding with conditional 'when' clause is correctly added to keybindings.json.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly fetches the VSCode keybindings.json file using vm_file
Metric correctly reads and parses the JSON file (handles both direct load and skip-first-line)
Expected values are semantically correct: key='ctrl+shift+f', command='workbench.view.explorer', when='!sideBarVisible'
All instruction requirements are covered in the verification (key binding, command, conditional clause)
Logic issue: The metric uses exact dict matching (expected in data), which will fail if the user adds extra optional fields to the keybinding (e.g., 'description', 'args')
The metric doesn't perform subset matching - it requires the keybinding dict to match exactly, which is overly strict for VSCode keybindings that support optional fields
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Modify check_json_keybindings to perform subset matching instead of exact dict matching: verify that all required fields (key, command, when) are present with correct values, but allow additional optional fields
Alternative: Iterate through the keybindings list and check if any entry has matching 'key', 'command', and 'when' fields, rather than checking exact dict equality

rule_validation_issues.msg: metric check_json_keybindings first parameter type (str) may not match getter get_vm_file return type (Union)
metric check_json_keybindings second parameter type (str) may not match expected.rules type (Dict)
